edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De resurrectione carnis, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.locus: On the Resurrection of the Flesh XXII
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Post haec, ad illas etiam Scripturas respiciendum est, quae non sinunt resurrectionem secundum animales istos, ne dixerim spiritales, aut hic jam in veritatis agnitione praesumi, aut ab excessu statim vitae vindicari. Cum enim et tempora totius spei fixa sint sacrosancto stylo, nec liceat eam ante constitui, quam in adventum, opinor, Christi, vota nostra suspirant in saeculi hujus occasum, in transitum mundi quoque ad diem Domini magnum, diem irae et retributionis, diem ultimum, et occultum, nec ulli praeter quam Patri notum, et tamen signis atque portentis, et concussionibus elementorum, et conflictationibus nationum praenotatum. Evolverem prophetias, si Dominus ipse tacuisset: nisi quod et prophetiae vox erant Domini: sed plus est, quod illas suo ore consignat. Interrogatus a discipulis. quando eventura essent, quae interim de templi exitu eruperant, ordinem temporum, primo Judaicorum usque ad excidium Hierusalem, communium, usque ad conclusionem saeculi, dirigit. Nam posteaquam edixit: Et tunc erit Hierusalem conculcatui nationibus, donec adimpleantur tempora nationum, allegendarum scilicet a Deo, et congregandarum cum reliquiis Israelis; inde jam in orbem et in saeculum praedicat, secundum Joelem, et Danielem, et universum concilium prophetarum, futura signa in sole et in luna et in stellis, conclusionem nationum cum stupore; sonitus maris, et motus refrigescentium hominum, prae metu et exspectatione eorum quae immineant orbi terrae. Virtutes enim, inquit, coelorum commovebuntur: et tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cum plurimo potentatu et gloria. Ubi autem coeperint ista fieri, emergetis, et elevabitis capita vestra, quod redemptio vestra appropinquarit. Et tamen adpropinquare eam dixit, non, adesse jam; et cum coeperint ista fieri, non, cum facta fuerint; quia cum facta fuerint, tunc aderit redemptio nostra, quae eo usque appropinquare dicitur, erigens interim et excitans animos ad proximum jam spei fructum. Cujus etiam parabola subtexitur tenerescentium arborum in caulem floris, et dehinc florem, frugis antecursorem: Ita et vos cum videritis omnia ista fieri, scitote in proximo esse regnum Dei. Vigilate ergo omni in tempore, ut digni habeamini effugere omnia ista, et stetis ante filium hominis: utique per resurrectionem, omnibus ante transactis. Ita, etsi in agnitione sacramenti fruticat, sed in Domini repraesentatione florescit atque frugescit. Quis ergo Dominum tam intempestive, tam acerbe excitavit jam ad dexteram Dei, ad confringendam terram secundum Esaiam, quae puto adhuc integra est? quis inimicos Christi jam subjecit pedibus ejus, secundum David, quasi velocior Patre, omni adhuc popularium coetu clamante, Christianos ad leonem? quis coelo descendentem Jesum talem conspexit, qualem ascendentem Apostoli viderant, secundum angelorum constitutum? Nulla ad hodiernum tribus ad tribum pectora caeciderunt, agnoscentes quem pupugerunt: nemo adhuc excepit Heliam: nemo adhuc fugit antichristum: nemo adhuc Babylonis exitum flevit. Et est jam qui resurrexerit nisi haereticus? Exiit plane jam de corporis sepulcro, etiam nunc febribus et ulceribus obnoxius; et conculcavit jam inimicos, etiam nunc luctari habens cum mundi potentibus. Et utique jam regnat, etiam nunc Caesari quae sunt Caesaris debens.
pass_a_gloss: After these things, it is to be looked at also to those Scriptures, which do not allow a resurrection according to those animals, or spiritual ones, neither to be presumed now in the recognition of truth, nor to be avenged immediately from the excess of life. For when also the times of all hope are fixed by a sacred stylus, and it is not permitted to establish it before, than in the advent, I think, of Christ, our vows sigh in the decline of this world, in the transition of the world also to the great day of the Lord, the day of wrath and retribution, the last day, and hidden, and known to no one except the Father, and yet foretold by signs and portents, and shakings of elements, and conflicts of nations. I would unfold the prophecies, if the Lord Himself had been silent: except that also the voice of prophecy was of the Lord: but it is more, that He Himself seals them with His own mouth. Having been asked by the disciples, when those things which had broken out about the exit of the temple would happen, He directs the order of times, first of the Jews up to the destruction of Jerusalem, common up to the conclusion of the world. For after He had said: And then Jerusalem will be trampled by nations, until the times of nations are fulfilled, namely those to be taken away by God, and gathered with the remains of Israel; from there now He preaches in the world and in the age, according to (Joel and Daniel and the whole council of prophets), future signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars, the conclusion of nations with amazement; the sound of the sea, and the movement of men growing cold, from fear and expectation of those things which threaten the earth. For the powers of the heavens, He says, will be moved: and then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with much power and glory. Where, however, these things begin to happen, you will emerge, and you will lift up your heads, because your redemption is approaching. And yet He said it is approaching, not that it is already present; and when these things begin to happen, not when they have been done; because when they have been done, then our redemption will be present, which is said to approach until then, raising and stirring up minds to the nearby fruit of hope. Whose parable is also subtly included, of trees growing tender in the branch of a flower, and from then on the flower, the forerunner of fruit: So also you, when you see all these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near. Therefore, watch at all times, so that you may be worthy to escape all these things, and stand before the Son of Man: certainly through resurrection, with all things having been transacted beforehand. So, although it flourishes in the recognition of the sacrament, but it blossoms and bears fruit in the representation of the Lord. Who, therefore, has so untimely, so harshly aroused the Lord to the right hand of God, to shatter the earth, which I think is still intact? Who has already subjected the enemies of Christ to His feet, as if faster than the Father, with every crowd of people still crying out, 'Christians to the lion'? Who has seen Jesus descending from heaven such as the Apostles saw Him ascending, according to the constitution of the angels? No hearts have yet fallen to the ground, tribe by tribe, recognizing the one they pierced: no one has yet received Elijah: no one has yet fled the antichrist: no one has yet wept over the exit of Babylon. And is there already one who has risen, unless he is a heretic? He has clearly already gone out of the tomb of the body, and is still now subject to fevers and ulcers; and he has already trampled his enemies, and is still now struggling with the powers of the world. And certainly he is already reigning, and is still now owing to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.

pass_b_english: We must now turn to those Scriptures, too, the ones that refuse to allow a resurrection modeled on these 'animals'—let alone spiritual ones—whether that resurrection is presumed right now in the recognition of truth or vindicated immediately at the departure from life. The times of our entire hope are fixed by a sacred stylus, and it is not permitted to set that hope before the Advent, I think, of Christ; our vows sigh for the decline of this age, for the world's transition to the great Day of the Lord, the day of wrath and retribution, the last day, hidden and known to no one except the Father—yet foretold by signs and portents, shakings of the elements, and conflicts of nations (Luke 21:24). I would unfold the prophecies if the Lord Himself had kept silent, except the prophetic voice was the Lord's own; but it is more that He seals them with His own mouth. When the disciples asked when the things that had burst forth at His departure from the Temple would happen, He laid out the order of times: first for the Jews until the destruction of Jerusalem, then for the nations until the conclusion of the age. For after He said, 'And then Jerusalem will be trampled by nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled'—that is, taken away by God and gathered with the remnant of Israel—from there He preaches to the world and the age, according to Joel and Daniel and the whole council of the prophets (Joel and Daniel), of future signs in the sun and moon and stars, the nations' conclusion with amazement; the roar of the sea, and the movement of men growing cold from fear and expectation of what threatens the earth. 'For the powers of the heavens will be shaken,' He says, 'and then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.' When these things begin to happen, you will stand up and lift your heads, because your redemption is drawing near. Yet He said it is drawing near, not that it is already here; and when these things begin, not when they are finished; because when they are finished, then our redemption will be present—the redemption that is said to approach until that moment, raising and stirring minds toward the nearby fruit of hope. Its parable is woven in, too: trees growing tender in the shoot of a blossom, and then the blossom, the forerunner of fruit. 'So also you, when you see all these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.' Therefore, stay awake at all times, so that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things and to stand before the Son of Man—certainly through the resurrection, with all things having been transacted beforehand. So, although it flourishes in the recognition of the sacrament, it blossoms and bears fruit in the representation of the Lord. Who, then, has so untimely and harshly roused the Lord to the right hand of God to shatter the earth—which I think is still intact? Who has already subjected Christ's enemies under His feet, as if faster than the Father, while every popular assembly still cries, 'Christians to the lion'? Who has seen Jesus descending from heaven such as the Apostles saw Him ascending, according to the angels' decree? No hearts have yet fallen to the ground, tribe by tribe, recognizing the One they pierced; no one has yet received Elijah; no one has yet fled the Antichrist; no one has yet wept over Babylon's exit. And is there already one who has risen, unless he is a heretic? He has clearly already come out of the body's tomb, yet still subject to fevers and ulcers; and he has already trampled his enemies, yet still struggling with the powers of the world. And he certainly reigns already, yet still owes Caesar what belongs to Caesar.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A preserves the syntax and nuances of the Latin (e.g., the distinction between 'approaching' and 'being present'). Pass B provides a fluent English rendering while maintaining the theological distinctions and adding necessary scripture citations (Luke 21:24, Joel, Daniel) that correspond to the Latin allusions. All clauses, including the rhetorical questions at the end, are accounted for.
